title: Minor burn first aid
summary: A friend touches a hot beaker. Give the right first aid, and know when it isn't minor.
sources: St John Ambulance: how to treat burns

scenes.narration: Your friend grabs a beaker that has just come off the tripod and yelps. The skin on two fingertips is red and stinging.

choices.label: That's a burn: act now
choices.feedback: Yes. Cooling a burn quickly reduces the damage.

choices.label: Shake it off, it'll be fine
choices.feedback: Cooling a burn straight away limits the damage. Don't wait.

scenes.narration: The red area is smaller than her palm and the skin isn't broken. She isn't feeling faint.

choices.label: It looks like a small, minor burn: start first aid and tell the teacher
choices.feedback: Right. Small, unbroken burns can be treated with first aid. Still tell the teacher.

choices.label: It's severe: call an ambulance
choices.feedback: This one is minor, but call 112 for large or deep burns, burns on the face or hands of a young child, or chemical or electrical burns.

scenes.narration: What first aid do you give?

choices.label: Cool it under cool or lukewarm running water for 20 minutes
choices.feedback: Correct. Cool running water for 20 minutes is the most important step.

choices.label: Hold ice on it
choices.feedback: Ice can damage the skin further. Use cool running water instead.

choices.label: Put butter or toothpaste on it
choices.feedback: Never use butter, oil or toothpaste: they trap heat and can cause infection.

scenes.narration: After 20 minutes the stinging has eased. A small blister is forming.

choices.label: Remove any rings, then cover loosely with cling film or a clean, non-fluffy dressing
choices.feedback: Yes. Remove jewellery before swelling, and cover to keep it clean.

choices.label: Pop the blister so it heals faster
choices.feedback: Don't burst blisters: they protect the skin underneath from infection.

choices.label: Wrap it in cotton wool
choices.feedback: Cotton wool sticks to burns. Use cling film or a non-fluffy dressing.

end-safe.text: The burn heals over the next week. Quick cooling made all the difference.

learn: Cool a burn under cool or lukewarm running water for 20 minutes.
Remove rings or watches near the burn before it swells.
Cover loosely with cling film or a clean non-fluffy dressing.
No ice, butter, oil or toothpaste; don't burst blisters.
Get medical help for large or deep burns, burns to the face, hands or genitals, chemical or electrical burns, or burns on young children.
disclaimer: Training only. This is not a substitute for emergency services or certified first-aid and fire-safety training. In a real emergency in India, call 112.
